scoring_note: Editorial musical hypotheses, not calibrated listeners. Specialist lane is proposed/inactive until routing and catalog activation are separately approved.

songs.title: Good Times
songs.rationale: The band makes repetition feel effortlessly communal, turning the rhythm section into a party invitation.

songs.title: I Feel Love
songs.rationale: Giorgio Moroder's synthetic pulse asks for surrender to an evolving machine, not a singalong band.

songs.title: Stayin' Alive
songs.rationale: Tough swagger and precision groove make confidence sound cool rather than explosive.

songs.title: I Will Survive
songs.rationale: Private betrayal becomes collective self-possession; a defining case of vulnerability rewritten as command.

songs.title: September
songs.rationale: A highly arranged communal celebration with no demand for suspense or menace.

songs.title: We Are Family
songs.rationale: Group identity is the refrain; the most literal test of pleasure becoming belonging.

songs.title: Disco Inferno
songs.rationale: Relentless, large-scale disco heat turns a celebration into near-dangerous spectacle.

songs.title: Get Down Tonight
songs.rationale: A simple rhythmic demand for the present moment, built for instant group movement.

songs.title: I'm Coming Out
songs.rationale: Nile Rodgers' groove underwrites a sweeping public declaration of becoming oneself.

songs.title: Shame
songs.rationale: Emotional doubt runs under buoyant dance-floor command, complicating uncomplicated disco joy.

songs.title: You Make Me Feel (Mighty Real)
songs.rationale: Vocal ecstasy and electronic acceleration make the floor a place of ecstatic public self-assertion.

songs.title: Turn the Beat Around
songs.rationale: A rhythmic command with percussion up front, where action matters more than patient atmosphere.

songs.title: Rock Your Baby
songs.rationale: Featherweight tenderness and a relaxed groove are a softer point of entry to disco pleasure.

songs.title: Supernature
songs.rationale: A cinematic, ominous synthetic epic takes disco beyond the social floor toward the uncanny.

songs.title: Don't Leave Me This Way
songs.rationale: A vulnerable, gospel-sized plea made massive by orchestration and dance-floor scale.

songs.title: Don't Stop 'Til You Get Enough
songs.rationale: An impeccably layered dance record that keeps developing around a light, assured vocal.

songs.title: Dancing Queen
songs.rationale: A cinematic shared memory packaged as an immediate, glamorous singalong.

songs.title: Love Hangover
songs.rationale: A languid intimate opening becomes a full disco release, making transformation the actual attraction.

pairings.phrase: The band runs the room, or the machine dreams the future?
pairings.why: Chic offers immediate human lockstep; Donna Summer invites a long synthetic, more abstract surrender.

pairings.phrase: Ride the impossible pulse, or strut in a perfect suit?
pairings.why: I Feel Love pushes disco toward machine immersion; Stayin' Alive gives the listener a character and a clear pose.

pairings.phrase: Walk out standing tall, or ask them not to go?
pairings.why: Gloria Gaynor makes recovery an act of command; Thelma Houston leaves the emotional request exposed.

pairings.phrase: A room full of old friends, or a disco on another planet?
pairings.why: Earth, Wind & Fire keep celebration immediate and welcoming; Cerrone brings distance, suspense and synthetic danger.

pairings.phrase: Belong to everybody, or dance with a private doubt?
pairings.why: Sister Sledge celebrate certainty and fellowship; Evelyn King lets embarrassment flicker through the groove.

pairings.phrase: Set the building on fire, or dim the lights for two?
pairings.why: The Trammps make disco huge and heated; George McCrae keeps it tender and almost weightless.

pairings.phrase: Get to the hook, or wait for the lights to change?
pairings.why: KC gives an immediate dance-floor command; Diana Ross takes the scenic route from intimacy to release.

pairings.phrase: Announce your arrival, or plead for one more chance?
pairings.why: Diana Ross projects independence; Thelma Houston transforms desire into an exposed appeal.

pairings.phrase: A whole new self, or just one terrific night out?
pairings.why: Sylvester turns pleasure into an enormous evolving declaration; KC stays in the present groove.

pairings.phrase: Hit the percussion now, or let desire become the beat?
pairings.why: Vicki Sue Robinson never lets rhythmic momentum wait; Love Hangover earns its explosion through a long transition.

pairings.phrase: Watch the arrangement keep inventing itself, or sing the moment forever?
pairings.why: Michael Jackson's groove keeps unfolding; ABBA offers a more self-contained, memory-making anthem.

pairings.phrase: Keep your cool, or make the whole room witness your comeback?
pairings.why: Bee Gees favor taut self-possession; Gloria Gaynor makes private reversal a larger shared event.
